name: Blue Owl

summary.text: Blue Owl Capital is an alternative asset manager formed when Owl Rock Capital Group (direct lending) and Dyal Capital Partners (GP capital solutions) combined with the SPAC Altimar Acquisition Corp. in a deal announced in December 2020, with more than $45 billion under management at announcement. In October 2025 Meta and funds managed by Blue Owl formed a joint venture to develop and own the Hyperion data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, with Blue Owl funds holding 80 percent and Meta 20 percent and the partners committing to fund their pro rata share of about $27 billion in development costs.

facts.claim: On October 21, 2025 Meta announced a joint venture with funds managed by Blue Owl Capital to develop and own the Hyperion data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana. Blue Owl-managed funds own 80 percent of the venture and Meta 20 percent; the parties committed to fund their pro rata share of approximately $27 billion in development costs, and Meta provides construction and property management services.
facts.quote: Funds managed by Blue Owl Capital will own an 80% interest in the joint venture, while Meta will retain the remaining 20% ownership.

sources.title: Meta Announces Joint Venture with Funds Managed by Blue Owl Capital to Develop Hyperion Data Center

facts.claim: Bisnow reported that Blue Owl funds contributed about $7 billion in cash to the Hyperion venture, that Meta received a one-time distribution of about $3 billion, that Meta signed leases for the campus and a residual value guarantee, and that Meta contributed land and construction-in-progress assets previously classified as held for sale. Bisnow described the structure as keeping the project's debt off Meta's balance sheet and as the largest such deal completed so far.
facts.quote: Blue Owl funds put roughly $7 billion in cash into the venture, and Meta took a one-time payout of about $3 billion.

sources.title: Meta Pushes Its Largest Data Center Project Off Its Books With $27B JV

facts.claim: Bisnow reported that much of Blue Owl's capital for the venture was funded by debt securities issued earlier in October 2025 through Pimco, rated A+ by S&P Global Ratings but yielding 6.58 percent at issue. Morgan Stanley was Meta's exclusive financial adviser and Kirkland & Ellis advised Blue Owl.
facts.quote: S&P Global Ratings gave the bonds an A+ investment-grade rating, yet they yielded 6.58% at issue, a rate usually tied to high-yield deals.

facts.claim: Blue Owl was formed by combining Owl Rock Capital Group and Dyal Capital Partners, a division of Neuberger Berman, with the SPAC Altimar Acquisition Corp. At announcement in December 2020 the combined firm had over $45.0 billion in assets under management: $23.7 billion in direct lending ($19.7 billion of it permanent capital) and $23.3 billion in GP Capital Solutions. Doug Ostrover became CEO, with Michael Rees and Marc Lipschultz as co-presidents.
facts.quote: The Owl Rock and Dyal businesses will be autonomous but complementary.

openQuestions: Site claim (Blind Pool): Meta financed Hyperion through a roughly $27B joint venture with Blue Owl, keeping the debt off its own balance sheet. The $27B joint venture is supported by Meta's release; the off-balance-sheet characterization is Bisnow's reporting, not a statement by either company.
Blue Owl's current (2025-2026) assets under management and its 10-K figures were not retrieved; only the 2020 formation figures were found.
The date and closing of the IPI Partners acquisition were not confirmed beyond the announcement title.
